title: The Sunday Market
setting: 7am. BTM 2nd Stage Sunday market. The road is half-blocked with tarp-roofed stalls. You stop in front of one with the best-looking tomatoes you've ever seen. The vendor aunty looks at you — once, top to bottom — then at her granddaughter, who hasn't looked up from her phone.

beats.native: ಬೇಕಾ ಸಾರ್? Tomato fresh. Kilo ಅರವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ.
beats.translit: bēkā sār? tomato fresh. kilo aravattu rūpāyi.
beats.en: Want some, sir? Tomatoes fresh. Sixty rupees a kilo.
beats.beat: the price she gives the office-bag people

beats.prompt: You look at the tomatoes. You say:

choices.native: ಅರವತ್ತು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಆಂಟಿ. ನಲವತ್ತು ಮಾಡಿ.
choices.translit: aravattu svalpa jāsti aunty. nalavattu māḍi.
choices.en: Sixty's a bit much, aunty. Make it forty.

beats.native: ಅಯ್ಯೋ ಸಾರ್, ನಲವತ್ತು ಗೆ ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತೆ? ಐವತ್ತು ಮಾಡಿ. ಫೈನಲ್.
beats.translit: ayyō sār, nalavattu-ge elli sigutte? aivattu māḍi. final.
beats.en: Aiyyo sir, where will you get them for forty? Make it fifty. Final.
beats.beat: already weighing them out, knowing how this ends

choices.native: ಸರಿ. ಐವತ್ತು. ಒಂದು kilo. ಮತ್ತೆ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಮೆಣಸಿನಕಾಯಿ.
choices.translit: sari. aivattu. ondu kilo. matte nālku meṇasinakāyi.
choices.en: Okay. Fifty. One kilo. And four chillies.

beats.native: ಮೆಣಸಿನಕಾಯಿ free ಸಾರ್. ಮುಂದಿನ ವಾರ ಬರ್ರೀ, ಬೇರೆ ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಬೆಲೆ ಕೊಡ್ತೀನಿ.
beats.translit: meṇasinakāyi free sār. mundina vāra barrī, bēre oḷḷe bele koḍtīni.
beats.en: Chillies on the house, sir. Come next week, I'll give you a better price.
beats.beat: the granddaughter looks up — first time since you arrived

beats.native: ನೀವು ಹೊಸದಾಗಿ ಬಂದಿದ್ದೀರಾ ಸಾರ್? ಮುಖ ನೋಡಿ ಗೊತ್ತಾಗುತ್ತೆ.
beats.translit: nīvu hosadāgi bandiddīrā sār? mukha nōḍi gottāgutte.
beats.en: You're new, aren't you, sir? It shows on the face.
beats.beat: tying up the bag, not looking up — but smiling

choices.native: ಹೌದು ಆಂಟಿ! Two weeks ಆಯ್ತು. ಪ್ರತಿ ಭಾನುವಾರ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ.
choices.translit: haudu aunty! two weeks āytu. prati bhānuvāra bartīni.
choices.en: Yes aunty! Two weeks now. I'll come every Sunday.
